current.text: He is a rookie and is projected to start at forward for Memphis next to Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant and Zach Edey.
Experts project about 30 to 32 minutes a night. Joe sees him as one of only two Grizzlies above 30 minutes. At 33 minutes he could be an easy top 50 player.
Memphis traded Ja Morant to Portland, and Ty Jerome is expected to start at point guard.
With Morant gone, he should take the first or second playmaking role in Memphis, and his assist rate should go up. He could lead the team in assists, but he is not expected to be a 30 usage player.
He averaged 17 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, a steal and a three in Summer League on 51% FG, 82% FT and 40% from three. He looked very good in his first preseason game.
Experts expect him to be the best fantasy rookie this season.

He should start slowly and struggle with efficiency early, probably ranking outside the top 70 at first. He should then play at a top 25 to 35 level in February and March, including the fantasy playoffs.
The newest call puts his fair draft range in the 60s. A Yahoo rank of 51 is a bit high but not terrible.
In an expert auction mock he went for 15 USD, which was exactly Josh's max bid.
Coach Tuomas Iisalo plays a very high pace with short stints and an 11 or 12 man rotation, which keeps minutes down across the roster.
Memphis plays 4 games in each of weeks 19, 20 and 21 for a March 28 end, and has only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.

durable.text: He does nearly everything: scoring, rebounds, assists, steals, solid free throws, good FG% and threes. He is an efficient scorer, an excellent passer and a scalable player.
He has limits as a rim protector and will likely lack blocks.
He plays more like a small forward than a center and has point forward potential.
He had a 30 usage rate at Duke with high assist numbers.
Turnovers are his weakest category for a forward. Rebounds are his best category, well above the average forward.
He is the number one dynasty rookie and an easy top 15 dynasty player.

note: The experts' fair range is around rank 60 to 65. Yahoo's average cost of 11.7 USD and the 15 USD mock price fit that better than Yahoo's 18 USD value. ESPN's 4 USD looks too low for a player expected to play at a top 35 level in our weeks 19 to 21. He also has a full 4-4-4 playoff schedule and few back-to-backs. He fits punt TO builds, but check early how many minutes he gets in Iisalo's short-stint rotation and how many threes he takes. Yahoo projects 1.3 threes per game and ESPN only 0.3, and that gap decides whether he helps or hurts your 3PM.
